## What a user of the old system will notice

**Closing a ticket will feel the same, respond faster under load.** Today, closing a ticket
sends a notification email synchronously — the request sits there for however long SMTP takes
(2s typical, up to the full 30s timeout on provider trouble, per `legacy/app/notify.py`'s own
docstring), and if the send fails outright the client gets a 500 even though the ticket WAS
closed (PB-001, ED-001). After the rewrite: the response comes back as soon as the ticket is
closed in the database; the notification goes out separately. Nobody should notice a functional
difference except a faster, more reliable response.

**Requesting a password reset: same experience, safer token underneath.** Legacy generates
reset tokens from `MD5(email + current time)` — predictable if you can guess the request window
(PB-002, ED-002). The rewrite swaps in a proper random token generator. The reset email still
arrives, the link still works the same way, the 30-minute expiry and the deliberately-identical
error message for "expired" vs. "wrong token" (that one's intentional, not a bug — see
`docs/domain/reset-token.md`) both carry forward unchanged.

## What holds unchanged (FIXED)

Everything else observed in the legacy code carries forward as-is unless a human rules
otherwise, INCLUDING behaviors that look like bugs: `GET /api/tickets/<id>` on a missing ticket
returns `200 {}`, not `404` (the legacy code comment itself says the UI depends on this); ticket
slugs can collide (no uniqueness enforced); an undocumented `X-Internal-Bypass` header skips the
reset rate limit; the `/internal/export/csv` endpoint ships even though a code comment suggests
nobody's called it since 2020. None of these were reported as problems by whoever commissioned
this rewrite, so none of them get "fixed" without a deliberate human decision — see
`docs/open-questions.md` for the live list of exactly that kind of decision waiting to be made.

## What's still genuinely open

Nine open questions exist (`docs/open-questions.md`), none blocking a WO outright but several
flagging gate review: whether timestamps should become UTC, whether the `users` table is dead
weight or secretly load-bearing, whether the app should have any auth layer at all, and — added
by the P9 adversarial audit, not the original draft — two malformed-request crash paths that a
Pydantic-based rewrite might not even be able to reproduce faithfully without deliberately
fighting the framework's own validation. See `decisions.md`'s "Still open" list.
